official.deadline_note: The 2026 Call for Applications required nominating agencies to submit the endorsed application forms to the Ministry by 27 March 2026; that edition has closed. No central date is published for the next edition - each nominating agency sets and communicates its own deadline in parallel with the Mauritian universities' admission windows.
official.application_cycle: Annual edition published by the Ministry (the 2026 edition call was issued in October 2025 with agency submissions closing 27 March 2026); the next edition is expected to follow the same annual cycle.
official.status_note: The 2026 edition call for applications was issued in October 2025 and its agency submission deadline (27 March 2026) has passed; the Ministry's MASS page now hosts the 2026 edition documents, with the next annual call expected later in the cycle.
official.tuition_coverage_note: 2026 Guidelines for Applicants: tuition and course-related costs are supported up to MUR 100,000 (SADC countries, local fees) or MUR 160,000 (non-SADC countries, international fees) on the published rate basis.
benefits: Tuition fees and course-related costs up to MUR 100,000 per year for SADC beneficiaries and MUR 160,000 per year for non-SADC beneficiaries
Monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 credited to the awardee's Mauritian bank account against evidence of attendance
Return airfare by the most economical route from the country of origin to Mauritius and back on successful completion
Student visa and provisional entry permit processed through the host institution and the Passport and Immigration Office
University application fee refunded to successful applicants
eligibility: Resident citizen of an African Union member state or an African Commonwealth country
For undergraduate programmes, above 18 years of age and not yet 26 by 1 January of the intake year
For MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD programmes, not yet 40 by 1 January of the intake year
Has already applied for a full-time on-campus Diploma, Degree, MPhil or PhD programme at a listed public higher education institution in Mauritius for the intake year
Qualifying examination result with an overall average of about 60% or 12/20, or the A-level equivalent, or an equivalent qualification
TOEFL 550 (paper), 213 (computer) or 79 (internet), or IELTS 5.5, where the language of instruction in the qualifying examination was not English
Not already holding an undergraduate degree when applying for an undergraduate programme
Not a self-financing African student already studying in Mauritius applying for the same programme level
requirements: Applications can only be made on the official application form and solely through the nominating agency responsible for scholarships in the applicant's country of citizenship; applications not processed through a nominating agency will not be considered
The nominating agency endorses Section 5 of the form and shortlists a maximum of fifteen eligible candidates before submitting them to the Ministry
Produce original educational certificates in Mauritius within two weeks of arrival
Undergo a medical check-up in a Mauritian public hospital within one month of arrival
Do not interrupt studies to take up employment, which terminates the award and requires refund of the whole amount paid
Inform the institution and the Ministry at least two weeks before any travel out of Mauritius
documents: Completed Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Application Form (filled electronically before printing)
Certified copy of the biodata page of the passport
Certified copies of educational certificates and transcripts
Conditional offer letter from a listed Mauritian public institution, or its application fee receipt
Medical certificate completed and stamped by a registered medical practitioner
selection_criteria: Selection is on merit after all attached conditions are satisfied and the host institution confirms a seat has been offered
Endorsement by the nominating agency (or the Ministry of Education where no agency exists) is mandatory
Candidates not informed of selection within six months of the application deadline should consider themselves not selected; the Ministry does not respond to individual queries
The final and binding decision rests with the Ministry, and the Government reserves the right to offer no scholarship at all following a call
coverage: Tuition fees and course-related costs up to the published annual cap (MUR 100,000 SADC / MUR 160,000 non-SADC)
Monthly living allowance of MUR 16,500 paid against institution attendance evidence
Return airfare by the most economical route, valid from the country of origin at the start of studies and back on successful completion
Visa and provisional entry permit arranged through the host institution
application_method: Obtain the application form and guidelines from the Ministry's MASS page and complete the form electronically
Apply in parallel to a listed Mauritian public higher education institution through its own admission window, obtaining a conditional offer or paying its application fee
Submit the completed form, endorsed by the nominating agency in your country of citizenship, so it reaches the Ministry by the agency deadline (27 March 2026 for the 2026 edition)
After award, the host institution applies for the student visa and provisional entry permit
On arrival, produce original certificates, undergo the medical check-up and open a Mauritian bank account for the allowance
official.application_route: Apply through the nominating agency in your country of citizenship (typically the Ministry of Education), after applying for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution; applications not processed through a nominating agency are not considered.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries.
official.international_eligibility: Designed for African students; age limits are 18-26 for undergraduate programmes and under 40 for MPhil/PhD programmes measured at 1 January of the intake year.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Study must be at a listed public higher education institution in Mauritius; the nominating agency in the applicant's own country is mandatory.
official.research_requirement: MPhil, MPhil/PhD and PhD applicants follow the separate Guidelines for Applicants for those programmes.
official.duration: Diploma up to 3 years; Degree up to 4 years; MPhil up to 2 years plus 6 months for thesis defence; MPhil/PhD up to 3 years plus 6 months for the transfer report plus 1 year plus 6 months for thesis defence; PhD up to 3 years plus 6 months
official.description: The Mauritius-Africa Scholarship Scheme is the Government of Mauritius scholarship for African students, run by the Ministry of Tertiary Education, Science and Research and open to resident citizens of African Union member states and African Commonwealth countries. The 2026 call funds Diploma, Bachelor's, MPhil and PhD study at public higher education institutions in Mauritius, supporting tuition fees and living expenses and covering return airfare.
official.english_requirement: Where the language of instruction in the qualifying examination was not English, a valid TOEFL result of 550 (paper-based), 213 (computer-based) or 79 (internet-based), or IELTS 5.5, or another acceptable proof of English proficiency is required; a virtual verbal interaction may be requested before the award.

verification.notes: The official 2026 Call for Applications and Guidelines for Applicants (undergraduate) PDFs were downloaded from tertiaryeducation.govmu.org and read directly on 2026-10-10: MUR 16,500 monthly living allowance, MUR 100,000 (SADC) / MUR 160,000 (non-SADC) fee caps, return airfare, the nominating-agency-only rule, the 27 March 2026 agency submission date and the TOEFL/IELTS thresholds were all confirmed in the documents.

applicant_utility.summary: MASS is Mauritius's government scholarship for African students: tuition covered up to MUR 100,000 (SADC) or MUR 160,000 (non-SADC) a year, a MUR 16,500 monthly living allowance paid against attendance, and return airfare - but the caps mean you should expect to top up fees and living costs yourself. The application only exists through your own country's nominating agency, and you must already be applying to a listed Mauritian public institution, so the real work happens in parallel at home and in Mauritius. Once on island, original certificates within two weeks and a medical check within one month are hard post-arrival conditions.
applicant_utility.best_fit: African Union and African Commonwealth citizens aged 18-26 (or under 40 for postgraduate study) who hold or are applying for a place at a listed Mauritian public institution and can secure agency endorsement at home.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify the nominating agency in your country (typically the Ministry of Education) and ask for its internal shortlist deadline, which falls before the Ministry's 27 March-style cut-off
Apply to a listed Mauritian public higher education institution in the same window and obtain a conditional offer or the application-fee receipt
Get birth certificate, passport biodata page, certificates and transcripts certified in advance
Have the medical certificate completed and stamped by a registered medical practitioner before submission
If your qualifying examination was not in English, book TOEFL (550/213/79) or IELTS 5.5 early
common_rejection_risks: Submitting directly to the Ministry instead of through the nominating agency, which disqualifies the file outright
Failing the age test measured at 1 January of the intake year (26 for undergraduate, 40 for postgraduate)
Missing the agency's shortlist round - each agency can endorse a maximum of fifteen candidates
Having no conditional offer and no application-fee receipt from a Mauritian institution
Assuming silence after six months means pending; the Ministry says treat it as not selected
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Fees above the MUR 100,000/160,000 annual cap, books, examination re-sits or repeats, and the gap between the MUR 16,500 monthly allowance and actual living costs; awardees are expected to arrive with funds for the one-way air ticket (refunded later on receipts) and at least USD 1,000 for the first three months.
document_audit: The application form must be completed electronically before printing - handwritten or altered forms risk rejection
Section 5 endorsement by the nominating agency is mandatory and must be complete
Original certificates must be produced in Mauritius within two weeks of arrival, so carry them, not just certified copies
Air ticket costs are refunded on arrival against original receipts, so keep every receipt from the journey
alerts: Taking up employment during the scholarship terminates the award and triggers refund of the whole amount paid
Any travel out of Mauritius needs at least two weeks' notice to the institution and the Ministry
The Ministry does not answer individual queries about selection outcomes
The Government reserves the right to offer no scholarship at all following a call
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the form, apply to a Mauritian institution, get the agency to endorse and transmit everything to the Ministry by its deadline, then await merit selection and the host institution's visa and entry-permit processing.
